verified.catalyst: Two dated binaries. First, the TensorWave 222 MW Project Matador lease must close by Oct 31 2026; it was pushed from Sep 30 because the guaranty is still being negotiated. Second, at the Oct 30 annual meeting the ousted founder Neugebauer (about 22% holder) has a 14a-8 proposal for an independent strategic review and governance changes.
verified.dated_milestone: 2026-10-30 annual meeting vote. Next: 2026-10-31 TensorWave lease closing deadline, with the guaranty still pending. Q3 10-Q due about mid-November.
verified.instrument: FRMI common (NASDAQ), $3.43 on 2026-10-12, at its 52-week low (52-week high $32.39).
verified.bloom_gates: G1 yes: named counterparty TensorWave TEX1 LLC on a 222 MW lease. G2 partial: a signed lease plus a First Amendment, but closing depends on an unsigned guaranty. Proposal 14a-8 is precatory (advisory only) and commits no transaction. G3 fails: no specific unpriced figure. The company is pre-revenue and the lease economics behind any re-rating are not disclosed.
verified.edge: L. Run-up from the pre-catalyst base is negative. The stock is down about 20% since the Sep 11 proposal filing, about 20% since the Sep 22 lease extension, and about 89% from its 52-week high. So the market is pricing failure, not success. Remaining capture is unquantifiable on a provenance basis. The only upside numbers are inherited sell-side figures (consensus PT $20.67, or +500%), and those are disallowed. The equity is about 2.1x book ($2.19B market cap vs $1.03B book) with no favorable-resolution value I can derive. Skew is negative: a failed guaranty or closing on Oct 31 strips out the only anchor tenant. A precatory review vote does not by itself create value.
verified.primary_source: Fermi/TensorWave First Amendment press release, Accesswire, 2026-09-22. Founder 14a-8 proposal press release, PRNewswire, 2026-09-11. Texas Business Court TRO denial press release, PRNewswire, 2026-09-17. FMP Q2 2026 balance sheet (filed 2026-08-14). FMP quote, 2026-10-12.
verified.analysis: Both events are real, dated and forward. However, the 14a-8 proposal is non-binding: the board won the TRO fight on Sep 17, and the court upheld its bylaws. The TensorWave closing is a financing-contingent binary at a pre-revenue developer that had only $62.5M cash at 6/30 against a $1.6B PP&E build and $731M of non-current liabilities, so a closing does not secure the funding. No preferred sits ahead of the common. Still, the equity waterfall cannot support a derived upside figure: there is no disclosed lease NPV, and the build is heavily capex-funded. So I am scoring the equity, not the event, under the cap of 4, and keeping it on WATCH for the Oct 31 closing print. Gap: the web-search budget was exhausted, so the guaranty status after Sep 22, current share count, debt terms in the Q2 10-Q notes and the proxy vote recommendations are unverified.

verified.catalyst: Fulcrum is doing an all-stock reverse merger with privately held Slate Medicines (announced 2026-08-17). Fulcrum holders end up with about 5.0% of the combined company and get a special cash dividend before closing. The deal needs a stockholder vote and is expected to close in Q4 2026.
verified.dated_milestone: Merger signed 2026-08-17 (GlobeNewswire/Reuters). Next: S-4 declared effective, then the FULC stockholder vote and the dividend record date, with closing guided to Q4 2026. The exact vote date and dividend size could not be confirmed.
verified.instrument: FULC common (Nasdaq), $3.77 on 2026-10-12. Buying now captures the pre-closing cash dividend plus a ~5% stub in Slate Medicines.
verified.bloom_gates: G1 yes: named counterparty, Slate Medicines, with a signed merger agreement. G2 yes: a concrete commitment to a pre-closing special cash dividend and a 5.0% ownership split. G3 only partial: the dividend size per share, the specific figure that matters here, is NOT verified (see analysis).
verified.edge: L. Run-up from the pre-catalyst base is about +25-33%: the post-pociredir low was $2.83 (52-week low), and the August pre-deal trading level was about $2.85-3.0, against $3.77 now. Remaining to the favorable value is about 0-10%. Net cash at 6/30/26 was $318.8M of cash and short-term investments minus $13.3M of total liabilities, or about $305M. Spread over about 76.3M shares (implied by FMP market cap and BlackRock's 8.82M shares = 11.57%), that is about $4.00/share. Burn was about $26M/quarter in Q2, and wind-down plus deal costs come on top, so cash at a Q4 close is likely about $3.5-3.8/share before the 5% Slate stub. A $3.77 price leaves roughly 0-10% if the stub is worth around $0.1-0.3/share. Most of the value is already priced in; the stock trades near liquidation value.

Merger: GlobeNewswire press release 2026-08-17 'Fulcrum Therapeutics and Slate Medicines Announce Merger Agreement' plus Reuters 2026-08-17; 5.0% ownership per Business Wire/Halper Sadeh 2026-08-17. verified.analysis: The event is real and forward-dated: a signed all-stock reverse merger with Slate Medicines, a pre-closing special dividend, and a Q4 2026 close subject to a vote. Several shareholder-rights firms are probing whether the 5% split is fair to FULC holders. Re-deriving value from the capital structure (no preferred stock, no debt, only $5.3M of leases, $318.8M cash at 6/30/26) gives about $4.00/share of net cash at June 30, falling toward about $3.5-3.8 by closing. At $3.77 the common is already priced at roughly cash plus a small option on the stub, so remaining capture is thin; the score is capped at 4 as mostly harvested. GAP: the exact dividend amount per share and the vote date could not be verified, because the web-search budget was used up and the GlobeNewswire press release returned 403. The "$245M deal" headline (Defense World/MarketBeat 2026-08-17) may be the dividend pool, which would be about $3.2/share. That needs confirming from the S-4/A before any upgrade.

verified.analysis: The deal is real and mostly unpriced: $12.61 implies New CommerceOne at ~$20/share against the flagged $27.6-$49.9, and only bank approvals remain. But the stock leg rests on an unlisted bank whose waterfall I could not re-derive (I did not reach the S-4/10-Q in my lookups). The Fed approval has no date and has already slipped past Q3, and the 2026-09 broker consensus is Reduce. The cash leg (64% of today's price) is a hard contractual floor once the deal closes. If it breaks, standalone GDOT falls back toward the ~$10 low (~-20%). So keep it on WATCH at 5 until a dated approval or a New CommerceOne pro-forma book value per share confirms the numerator. GAP: web search budget was exhausted; regulatory status comes only from FMP news (latest 2026-08-18 Zacks: approvals still pending), and I could not confirm whether anything happened between Sept and Oct.
